text:
Ashley Nguyen: Hey — spotting a regression after the Llama2x 13B safetensors conversion. p50 looks fine but p99 token latency jumped ~30% after the new HF parse changes. Anyone seen this pattern?

Mike C: Is this on-hosted or dedicated?

Ashley Nguyen: Dedicated infra, repro on both prod-dedicated and local perf bench. Small chat requests (~20 tokens). Repro profile attached below.

Ashley Nguyen: ```
profile: kernel_select: chosen=rope_fused_fp16_v2
latency: p50=28ms p95=110ms p99=240ms
kv_cache: steady_size=512MB evictions=0
notes: tail spikes ~200-300ms for cold prefixes
```

Raj Patel: Hmm. That kernel_select looks right-ish, but ropE params could be off so we hit prefetch/gating thrash. Did conversion set rotary scaling / head dim correctly?

Ashley Nguyen: HF config we used (sanitized):
```json
{"hidden_size": 8192, "num_attention_heads": 64, "rotary_pct": 0.25, "rotary_emb_dim": 64}
```

Diana L: Wait, rotary_emb_dim=64 with 64 heads -> head_dim=128? That math doesn't add up. If hidden_size/head != head_dim*heads, kernel chooses fallback path.

Mike C: Can you dump the safetensors metadata? I suspect the converter wrote metadata['rotary_scaling'] as a string or left it out. Our kernel selector expects numeric "rope_scale" or fallback to heuristic.

Ashley Nguyen: safetensors meta snippet: ```
{ "format": "safetensors", "metadata": { "rotary_emb": "64", "rotary_scale": "auto" } }
```

Raj Patel: There's the bug — "rotary_emb" is string -> our hfparse treats that as missing and computes head_dim = hidden_size/num_heads = 128, but downstream conversion code used rotary_emb=64 -> mismatch. Kernel hysteresis saw inconsistent head_dim across batches and switched kernels midstream -> thrash.

Diana L: That would explain p99 spikes due to kernel rebind + KV cache warmup. When kernel changes, KV layout expected dims differ -> temp extra copies and eviction behavior.

Mike C: Quick mitigation: patch hfparse to coerce numeric strings in metadata, and add a sanity check to recompute rotary_emb from head_dim if provided values conflict. Example one-liner:```python
meta['rotary_emb'] = int(meta.get('rotary_emb') or meta.get('rotary_emb_dim') or hidden_size//num_heads)
```

Ashley Nguyen: Tested that locally — p99 drops back to baseline. But we need a fix in conversion script too; some historical converters write strings.

Raj Patel: I'll add a CI lint in the converter repo to assert metadata types and roundtrip the safetensors header. Also add unit test where hfconfig has mismatched fields to ensure we warn+normalize.

deploy-bot: Deploy queue: canary patch+hfparse coercion created (PR #4821). Staging run scheduled.

Diana L: Even with coercion we should hard-fail on impossible combos (e.g., rotary_emb > hidden_size). Add an opt-in tolerance check and an automatic normalization note in the model onboarding log.

Mike C: Also add a metric: kernel_switch_count per request_id to watch for mid-request kernel rebinds. If >0 we alert and route to safe kernel. That will buy time for conversion fixes.

Ashley Nguyen: Good idea. I saw 1.2 kernel_switch_count spikes correlating with p99 windows.

Raj Patel: I'll wire kernel_switch_count into the RouteStats exporter. Also plan: when kernel_switch_count > 0 for a model we mark it as "config_unsafe" in the console and block dedicated rollouts.

ci-bot: Staging CI passed for PR #4821, tests=2138, flaky=1; bench regression test shows p99 restored within 5% of baseline.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to 3 nodes (redwood-dedicated-us-west-2). Monitoring for 30m.

Ashley Nguyen: Canary looks clean so far. p99 back to normal, kernel_switch_count=0. Will follow up tomorrow with full conversion sweep. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Raj Patel: Follow-up actions: 1) merge hfparse coercion + converter lint 2) add kernel_switch_count alert 3) add docs section on safetensors metadata expectations 4) batch test matrix that includes small short-prompts to catch eviction/kernels thrash.

Diana L: I'll own the batch test matrix. Putting a quick checklist in the onboarding doc.

Ashley Nguyen: Closing loop: primary root cause = inconsistent rotary metadata (string vs int) + converter mismatch -> kernel selector hysteresis -> KV cache/kernel warmup thrash -> p99 regression. Patch + canary fixed it.

Mike C: Nice catch.

Ashley Nguyen: Filing a short postmortem + remediation checklist later today.
